questions.question:
There are four important event about life of Buddha and their related places are mention below: Match the column 1 and column II and select the correct Answer:
Column I Column II
(A) Birth                  (1) Sarnath
(B) Enlightenment   (2) Bodhgaya
(C) First Sermon      (3) Lumbini
(D) Death                (4) Kushinagar
Codes:
A B C D
questions.explanation:
Gautama Buddha was the founder of Buddhism. His life is associated with four important events, which took place at four different locations.

Birth – Lumbini: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini, which is located in present-day Nepal. His childhood name was Siddhartha Gautama. His father was King Suddhodana and his mother was Queen Maya.

Enlightenment – Bodhgaya: Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodhgaya in Bihar while meditating under the Bodhi tree. After attaining enlightenment, Siddhartha became known as Buddha, meaning "The Enlightened One".

First Sermon – Sarnath: After attaining enlightenment, Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh. This event is known as Dharmachakra Pravartana, meaning the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma. He taught the Four Noble Truths and the Middle Path.

Death – Kushinagar: Gautama Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar in Uttar Pradesh at approximately 80 years of age. Mahaparinirvana refers to his final passing away.

Therefore, the correct matching is A–3, B–2, C–1 and D–4.

questions.question: The palace of Chandragupta in Patliputra was made of:
questions.explanation:
The place of Chandragupta, situated at Patliputra, was made mainly of wood.
• The palace complex of Chandragupta was built using wood, which was a common material for construction during that time period.
• The palace was described as a magnificent structure, with multiple floors and spacious rooms, and was said to have housed thousands of people.

questions.question: At the time of Huen Tsang visits in India which town was famous for production of cotton cloths?
questions.explanation:
At the time of Huen Tsang’s visit to India, the town that was famous for the production of cotton cloths was Mathura.
• Hiuen Tsang was a Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled from China to India during the reign of King Harshavardhana.

questions.question: Patna as a provincial capital was made by:
questions.explanation:
Patna was made the provincial capital by Sher Shah Suri.
• Sher Shah Suri ascended the throne of Delhi after defeating the Mughal ruler Humayun in the battle of Chausa in 1539 and Kannauj in 1540.
• In the year 1541 AD, its name was changed from Pataliputra to Patna.

questions.question: Where was the gold miners of Bihar situated in the 17th century?
questions.explanation: According to the English traveller Rolf Finch, there is evidence of a gold mine in Patna in the 17th century.

questions.question: Who was the foremost representative of ‘Neo Hinduism’ of late 19th century?
questions.explanation:
The foremost representative of “Neo Hinduism” of the late 19th century was Swami Vivekananda.
• He was a disciple of Ramakrishna Paramhansa and after becoming a monk, he embarked on extensive travels throughout India and the West.

questions.question: Home Rule Movement was a new chapter in freedom struggle of India, because:
options: It paved the way of self government to the country
A joint struggle started by Hindus and Musalmans
It united the extremists and Liberals
questions.explanation:
Hindus and Muslims started a joint struggle for self-rule through the Home Rule Movement.
• The Home Rule League was founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant in April 1916 and September 1916 respectively.
• The movement was unique in that it brought together both extremist and moderate leaders, as well as Hindus and Muslims, who were previously divided into political and religious lines, at the Lucknow session of the Congress.

questions.question: The Ghadar Party was founded in year:
questions.explanation:
The Ghadar Party was founded in the year 1913.
• The Ghadar Party was a political revolutionary organization founded by migrant Indians in San Francisco (USA).
• The primary goal of the party was to secure India’s independence from British rule.
• Sohan Singh, Kartar Singh, Abdul Mohammad Barkatullah and Rashbehari Bose were among the prominent leaders who contributed to expanding the organization to the United States and Canada.

questions.question: The slogan ‘Do or die’ related to:
questions.explanation:
The slogan ‘Do or die’ was given by Gandhiji during the Quit India Movement of 1942.
• The Quit India Movement, also known as the August Kranti Movement began on August 8, 1942.

questions.question: Who was the secretary of Mahatma Gandhi at Noakhali Period?
questions.explanation:
The secretary of Mahatma Gandhi during the Noakhali period was Pyarelal Nayar.
• Pyarelal played a significant role in the Noakhali movement, which was launched by Gandhi in 1946 to promote communal harmony and end violence between Hindus and Muslims in the Noakhali district of Bengal.

options: As a member of executive council of Congress
questions.explanation:
Jai Prakash Narayan was recognized as a national leader in the year 1942 during the Quit India Movement.
• In this movement, he launched a campaign of rebellion against the British by establishing a secret organization.

questions.question: Who was the last governor General of Independent India?
questions.explanation:
C. Rajgopalachari was the last Governor- General of Independent India.
• Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India and the first Governor General of independent India.
• C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) was the first and last Indian Governor General of independent India.

questions.question: Cause of the resurgence of revolutionary activities in Indian politics in the period of 1923-28 was:
options: Increasing impact of leaders like Hardyal and Lajpat Rai
Withdrawal of non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhiji
Rejection of Indian demands by the English.
questions.explanation:
The main reason for the revival of revolutionary activities in Indian politics during 1923-28 was the withdrawal of the non-cooperation movement by Gandhiji after the Chauri Chaura incident (5 February 1922).
• The harsh repressive response of the British government to suppress the non-cooperation movement, mainly the British government’s rejection of Indian demands, led to disillusionment and despair among many Indian nationalists.

questions.question: After failure of Civil Disobedience Movement Gandhiji recognize:
questions.explanation:
• After the failure of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1932, Gandhiji gave importance to constructive programmes, such as spinning yarn, spinning wheels etc.
• These constructive programs aimed to address social and economic issues such as poverty, untouchability and education, and were seen as a way of empowering Indians to take control of their own lives and communities.

questions.question: Which is the reason of failure of 1857 revolt?
options: The lack of any general plan and central organisation
questions.explanation:
The main reason for failure of 1857 revolt was the lack of any general plan and central organization.
• The failure of the rebellion is attributed to several factors, including the lack of a single leader, the limited region of its impact, the non-participation of landlords, unity and support of all rulers and castes and poor coordination.

questions.question: Who led Bardoli Satyagraha?
questions.explanation:
The Bardoli Satyagraha was a peasant movement led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in 1928.
• The peasants of Bardoli, located in Gujarat, did a satyagraha under the leadership of Vallabh Bhai Patel in protest against the increased tax by the government.
• It was during this Satyagraha that the women of Bardoli gave Vallabhbhai Patel the title of “Sardar”, which means leader or chief.

questions.question: After passing Quit India Resolution, Gandhiji was lodged in:
questions.explanation:
After passing the Quit India Movement Resolution, Gandhiji was lodged in the Aga Khan Palace in Pune.

questions.question: Which issues was the reason for failure of Second Round Table conference?
questions.explanation:
Communal Representation was the reason for failure of Second Round Table conference.
• The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in 1931 to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
• Mahatma Gandhi was the sole representative of Congress at the conference.
• The conference focused mostly on communal questions and the representation of minorities in the legislature at the centre and provinces.
• The British government did not agree to grant India Dominion status, which was a key demand of the Indian leaders.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress protested against Rowlatt Act because its aim was:
options: To limit Civil Liberty of Indians
To broaden the issue of communal representative
To arrest a national leader of treason
questions.explanation:
The Rowlatt Act was implemented to limit the rights of Indian citizens.
• The Rowlatt Act of 1919, was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919.
• This act granted the British government the authority to arrest anyone suspected of terrorist activity and detain them for up to two years without trial.
• It also allowed the police to conduct searches without a warrant and severely curtailed press freedom.

questions.question: Swami Vivekananda founded Ramkrishna Mission in the year:
questions.explanation:
Swami Vivekananda, a chief follower of Ramakrishna Paramhansa, established the ‘Ramakrishna Math’ at Belur near Calcutta in 1896-97.
• The Ramakrishna Mission is a Hindu spiritual and religious organization, also known as the Vedanta movement, which takes its inspiration from the teachings of the Indian spiritual master, Ramakrishna Paramahansa.
• The primary philosophy promoted by the organization is Advaita Vedanta, a Hindu philosophy.

questions.question: Who was elected as a President of Indian National Congress in 1938?
questions.explanation: In 1938 at Haripura Congress annual session, Subhash Chandra Bose was elected the President of the Indian National Congress.

questions.question: Which of the following has ended to dual government of Bengal?
questions.explanation:
The Dual government system was abolished in the year 1772 by Warren Hastings.
• The Dual Government system was introduced in Bengal by the British East India Company under the leadership of Robert Clive.

questions.question: Ranjit Singh had received the famous Kohinoor diamond from:
questions.explanation: Ranjit Singh, the ruler of Punjab, had received the famous Kohinoor diamond from Shah Shuja, the ruler of Afghanistan.

questions.question: Who was the first Maratha Sardar to accept Subsidiary Alliance of Lord Wellesley?

questions.question: Who was the founder of All India Muslim League?
questions.explanation:
The ‘Muslim League was founded under the leadership of Agha Khan.
• A group of Muslims under the leadership of Agha Khan met Viceroy Lord Minto in Shimla in October 1906.
• This delegation requested the Viceroy that a separate communal election system should be made for Muslims for provincial, central and local elections.
• Minto fully supported their demand, as a result of which the ‘Muslim League’ was established in Dhaka on December 30, 1906.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Atmiya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Atmiya Sabha was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta in the year 1814 AD to fight against idolatry, caste rigidity, rituals and other social evils.

questions.question: Which year Brahma Samaj was founded?
questions.explanation:
The Brahmo Samaj was founded on August 20, 1828, in Calcutta as a reform movement by Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Dwarkanath Tagore.
• The organization emphasized monotheism and rejected the idea of idol worship and caste distinctions.
• The Brahmo Samaj played an important role in advocating women’s rights and promoting gender equality, including opposing the practice of child marriage and advocating widow remarriage.

questions.question: Which year Gorakshini Sabha were established in Bihar to prohibit cow-slaughting?

questions.question: Which year Orissa was separated from Bihar?

questions.question: Chhotanagpur tenancy Act was passed in:
questions.explanation:

• The act prohibited the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals, except with the permission of the Deputy Commissioner.

questions.question: What is the nature of Planning Commission?

questions.question: The Chairman of the Planning Commission of India is:

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
questions.explanation: On November 26, 1949, the Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly. It came into effect on January 26, 1950, and is celebrated as Republic Day in India.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties are added by:
questions.explanation:
The 42nd Amendment Act, of 1976 added the Fundamental Duties to the Constitution on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
• Article 51-A under Part lV-A of the Constitution describes the fundamental duties.
• Initially, 10 fundamental duties were added but through the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 11th fundamental duty was added.

questions.question: A Minister of Union Council of Minister is responsible for:
questions.explanation:
As per Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Article 75 deals with:
• The Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the PM.
• The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. However The ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.question: The President of India has no power to:
questions.explanation:
The President of India does not have the power to remove the Justices of Courts.
• The power to remove a judge rests with the Parliament of India, which can impeach a judge for proven misbehaviour or incapacity.

questions.question: Rajya Sabha is called Permanent House, because:
options: All members are members for life long
Some members retire in every two years
questions.explanation:
Rajya Sabha is known as the permanent house of the Parliament because it is never completely dissolved.
• Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament, which represents the states and union territories of India.

questions.question:
According to Constitution of India, Legislatures of states includes:
I. Legislative Council and Governor
II. Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
III. Legislative Assembly and Governor
IV. Governor, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council where it exists
Select the correct code.
questions.explanation:
According to the Constitution of India, the Legislature of a State consists of the Governor, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council (where it exists).
• As of 2023, only six states in India have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: The word ‘Cabinet of Ministers’ is used one time in Constitution, where:
questions.explanation: The word ‘Cabinet’ is used only once in the Constitution under Article 352(3), when the President, in consultation with the Cabinet, declares the emergency. Article 352 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to declare a National Emergency in the country when there is a threat to the security of the country or any part of it due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

questions.question: Indian Citizenship cannot be achieved by:
options: By incorporation of a new territory into the Indian Union
By deposition of Wealth in Indian banks
questions.explanation: According to the Citizenship Act, of 1955, “Indian citizenship can be acquired by birth, by naturali- zation, by registration, by incorporation of any territory”. Indian Citizenship cannot be acquired by illegal means such as entering the country without valid travel docu- ments, overstaying the period of authorized stay, or vio- lating the terms and conditions of the visa.

questions.question: In general election age of voting is decreased to 18 years from 21 years by:
questions.explanation: By the 61st Constitutional Amendment in 1989, the age limit for voting in general elections was reduced from 21 years to 18 years.

questions.question: How many people are nominated in Rajya Sabha by the President?
questions.explanation:
The President has the power to nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.
• The members nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha are selected based on of their expertise and practical experience in various fields such as literature, arts, science and social services.

questions.question: The earth revolves around the Sun is about:
questions.explanation: It takes 365 days, 5 hours, 48 minutes and 46 seconds for the Earth to revolve around the Sun, that is, 365.25 days.

questions.question: The hottest planet in the solar system is:
questions.explanation:
Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System. Its temperature is about 462°C.
• Venus has a very thick atmosphere of carbon dioxide.
• The atmosphere traps heat, preventing it from escaping back into the atmosphere.

questions.question: The longest mountain system in the world is:
questions.explanation:
The Andes mountain range is the world’s longest mountain range.
• It is located in South America.
• It crosses the borders of 7 countries: Venezuela, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Argentina.

questions.question: The biggest delta of the world is formed by:
questions.explanation:
The Ganga Brahmaputra Delta is the largest in the world.
• The total land area covered by it is around 75,000 square kilometers.
• It is located in India and Bangladesh.
• The delta is also known as the Sundarbans Delta or Bengal Delta.

questions.question: The cotton industry is dependent on raw-materials:
questions.explanation:
The cotton industry (cotton textile industry) is based on weight loss-based raw materials.
• In India, cotton is a crucial cash crop that holds significant economic value.
• India is the world’s second-largest producer of cotton after China.
• Gujarat is the largest producer of cotton in India.

questions.question: In comparison to female, male has high colour blindness, because:
options: They spend more time out of the home
questions.explanation:
Colour blindness is more common in men than women because the responsible genes are located on the X chromosome.
• Colour blindness is a genetic condition that affects an individual’s ability to distinguish between different colours.
• Since males have only one X chromosome, they are more likely to develop colour blindness if they inherit a defective gene on that chromosome.

questions.question: The chances of desert on the earth are near:
questions.explanation:
The probability of desert on earth is more near 23° latitude.
• Deserts are typically found in regions where the annual precipitation is low and evaporation rates are high.
• Around 23 degrees latitude north and south of the equator, there is a belt of dry, subtropical air known as the horse latitudes or subtropical highs.
• This area is associated with persistent high pressure, which inhibits the formation of clouds and results in low precipitation, making it a prime location for desert formation. Examples of deserts in this region include the Sahara Desert in Africa, the Arabian Desert in the Middle East, and the Mojave Desert in North America.

questions.question: The height of ozone layer is:
questions.explanation:
The ozone layer extends from approximately 10 to 50 kilometres (6 to 31 miles) above the Earth’s surface.
• The ozone layer is a region in the upper atmosphere that contains high concentrations of ozone molecules.
• The ozone layer is important for human survival as it absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.
• Ultraviolet radiation can cause skin cancer and other.

questions.question: In winter season, if we touch an iron block and wood block in the morning, then we feel iron block is colder than wooden block, because
options: Temperature of iron block is less than wooden block
Iron is good conductor of heat than wood
Iron is bad conductor of heat than wood
Iron block has more weight than wooden block
questions.explanation:
Iron is a good conductor of heat than wood.
• Metals are better conductors of heat than wood, which means they can transfer heat more efficiently from our bodies to their cold surfaces.
• This leads to our hands losing heat rapidly, making us feel colder when touching a cold metal surface.

questions.question: Isotope of any atomic nucleus is that nucleus which has:
options: Number of neutrons are same but numbers of protons are different
Number of protons are same but numbers of neutrons are different
Number of protons and neutrons are same
Number of protons and neutrons are different
questions.explanation: Atoms of the same element that contain the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons, are known as isotopes.

questions.question: The active chemical in mosquito repellent is:
questions.explanation: Allethrin is the synthetic insecticide used mainly in almost all mosquito repellent coils. Citronella oil is also mixed in some quills with it.

questions.question: The surface of the earth which is covered by water is about: 1 1 2 3
questions.explanation:
Approximately three-fourths of the Earth’s surface is covered by water, which is about 71% of the Earth’s surface.
• The remaining 29% is land, which includes continents and islands.

questions.question: Which constellation, stars directed towards pole stars?
questions.explanation: The Great Bear constellation whose stars point towards the Pole Star (Northern Hemisphere) These stars are in square and oblique lines and look like the shape of a kite.

questions.question: Heavy water is that water which:
options: Contain undissolved salt of Ca and K
Place of hydrogen is replaced by its isotope
Place of Oxygen is replaced by its isotope
questions.explanation:
In heavy water, the hydrogen atoms are replaced by deuterium atoms, resulting in the chemical formula D O.
• Heavy water is water that is composed of the isotope deuterium.
• It is also known as deuterium oxide.

questions.question: The fundamentals of nucleus of an atom are:
questions.explanation:
The basic components of an atom’s nucleus consist of protons and neutrons.
• The nucleus is the central part of an atom, and it contains positively charged protons and neutral neutrons, held together by the strong nuclear force.

questions.question: The Number of bones in human body at the age of 20 years, about:
questions.explanation:
There are a total of 206 bones in the body of an adult human being.
• At birth, the human body has approx 300 bones, but some of these bones fuse together as the body develops, resulting in the adult human body having around 206 bones.

questions.question: The disease spread by HIV is:
questions.explanation:
The disease spread by HIV is AIDS, which stands for Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome.
• HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) is a virus that can infect and damage the immune system, rendering the body susceptible to infections and illnesses.
• The virus is mainly transmitted through the exchange of bodily fluids, including blood, semen, vaginal secretions, and breast milk.

questions.explanation: FAST is not a language of computers. It is not a commonly used programming language.

questions.question: On the Celsius Scale, the normal temperature of human body will be:
questions.explanation: On the Celsius Scale, the normal temperature of the human body is approximately 36.9° Celsius. This temperature is equivalent to 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) on the Fahrenheit scale,

questions.question:
The biggest planet in the solar system is:
(a) Earth (b) Mars (b) Jupiter (d) Saturn
questions.explanation:
The largest planet in the Solar System is Jupiter.
• The largest planet Jupiter has a radius of 69,911 km.
• Jupiter is the largest planet second largest planet is Saturn.
• The smallest planet in the Solar System is Mercury, whose radius is 2439.7 km.

questions.question: In air which gas has the maximum amount?
questions.explanation: By volume, the Earth’s atmosphere is composed of approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.93% argon, 0.03% carbon dioxide, and amounts of other gases.

questions.question: Extra-peninsular mountain of India formed in:
questions.explanation:
The extra-peninsular mountains of India were formed in the Palaeozoic era.
• The extra-peninsular mountains of India were primarily formed as a result of the collision between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate.
• This collision began around 50 million years ago and is ongoing, resulting in the ongoing uplift of the Himalayas.

questions.question: The old alluvial soil of the plain of Ganga is called:
questions.explanation:
The old alluvial soil of the plain of Ganga is called Bangar soil.

questions.question: The sum of three prime numbers is 100, in which one number is greater by 36 to other. Highest prime number is:
questions.explanation: The sum of three prime numbers can only be even if one of the prime numbers is even, the only prime number that is even is 2. So, the sum of the other two prime numbers must be 98. x + x + 36 = 98 ⇒ 2x = 62 ⇒ x = 31 Numbers are 2, 31 and 67. Hence, the highest prime number in this case is 67.

questions.question: Series 1, 2, 5, ......., 677, the missing number is:
